The empire network, and one figure per territory

Companion to the core figures. Nothing here is subsetted: figure 4 is every firm in the interlock graph and each territory figure is that territory's complete graph. Read them for shape and composition, not for individual firms — at this density the ink is the message.

Figure 4 — every firm, every interlock

All 5,959 firms that share at least one director with another, and all 78,530 interlocks between them. The giant component holds 5,871 of them (98.5%); the rest are in the strip below the rule. Colour is the firm's first territory, folded to the three largest — the question the figure answers is whether those three separate or interleave.

Empire (transversal) (30%)Indochina (16%)Morocco (13%)Other territory

A firm absent here is not a firm without directors — it is a firm the collection never shows sharing one. Coverage is very uneven by territory and period; see METHODOLOGY §6.

Figure 5 — the empire as a network of territories

The same data aggregated: each cell is the number of directors holding board seats in both territories, for the 54 territories with at least eight directors. A matrix rather than a node-link diagram because at this level the graph is small and nearly complete, where a node-link diagram degenerates into a scribble. The diagonal is outlined, not filled — a territory does not share directors with itself.

Shading steps by rank, not linearly — the counts are heavily skewed, so a linear ramp would leave every pair but the top few in the palest step. Hover a cell for the actual number. Multi-territory firms put their whole board into every territory they are listed in, which is exactly the tie being counted: a Paris-registered firm operating in Morocco and Indochina links the two.

One figure per territory

Each is that territory's complete interlock graph, drawn from its own bundle in data/by_country/. One hue, so no legend: the heading names the series. Counts under each heading are for that territory alone.

No figure for Mozambique, Peru, Abyssinia (Ethiopia), Russia, Dutch Guiana (Suriname), Siam (Thailand), Albania, Mauritania, Chad, Nigeria, Georgia — each has firms in the dataset but no two of them share a director, so there is no network to draw. That is a statement about the collection's coverage, not about the territory.
